The token is an RS256 access token issued by the Kobana authorization server (`account.kobana.com.br`), with `aud` equal to `https://api.dashboards.kobana.com.br` and a required `exp`. The `org` claim (the Kobana account) is what scopes the data and is required too; `sub` is the **person** and is carried for audit. This API only verifies tokens — it issues none. The `scope` claim is enforced too, a single access level per operation: a `GET` needs `read`, `write` or `all`; a `DELETE` needs `delete` or `all`; the bulk exports need `export` or `all` and the imports `import` or `all`; any other method needs `write` or `all` — always within the `dashboards/{group}` resources the token carries. Otherwise the answer is `403 insufficient_scope`, with `{ required, granted }` in `details`. A token issued to a **person** (`src` `user` or `oauth`) is also bounded by what that person may do in the dashboard: the operation needs the matching permission of their role (otherwise `403 insufficient_permission`, with `{ required }` in `details`), and someone who is not an active member of the organization is refused. A person token whose `sub` this app cannot identify returns `401 invalid_token`. Machine tokens (`src` `system` or `api`) act for the organization.

## Authentication

Every request carries the token, which says which **organization** you are. When the organization has more than one **workspace**, it also carries the `X-Workspace-Id` header, which says which of them to act on.

```
Authorization: Bearer <token>
X-Workspace-Id: <workspace id or public_id>
```

### The token

A **Kobana Account** access token: a JWT signed **RS256** by the Kobana authorization server (`account.kobana.com.br`). This API only verifies it — it issues no tokens.

| Claim | Role |
| :--- | :--- |
| **`org`** | **The tenant.** The Kobana account the token acts for — what decides which data the token reaches. Required. |
| `sub` | The **person** who consented. It is there for audit and scopes **nothing**. |
| `scope` | Space-separated list (e.g. `dashboards/users read write`): the resources the token reaches and the access levels within them — see **Scopes and access levels**, below. |
| `jti` | Token identifier, used for revocation. |
| `iss` / `aud` / `exp` | Issuer, audience and expiry (required). |

⚠️ The tenant is `org`, never `sub`. They are different identifier spaces: a person id never matches an organization, so a token without `org` is refused.

### Scopes and access levels

The token's `scope` has two axes, and an operation needs both:

- **Resource** — how far the token reaches: `dashboards/{group}`, one of ten groups (`builder`, `users`, `portal`, `connectors`, `entities`, `assets`, `ai`, `workspaces`, `members`, `admin`), or `dashboards/all` for all of them. A route's group comes from the first segment of its path. A token with no `dashboards/…` scope at all (an integration token) reaches the whole app and counts by its access level alone.
- **Access level** — what the token may do within that reach. There are six, and **none stands in for another**:

| Level | Grants |
| :--- | :--- |
| `read` | Reading (`GET`). `write` and `all` read too. |
| `write` | Creating and changing (`POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`). It does not delete, import or export. |
| `delete` | Deleting — every `DELETE`, single or bulk, and the purge (`DELETE /data_purges`). |
| `import` | Bringing data in in bulk: `POST /imports`, `POST /entities/:id/records/import`, `POST /workspaces/import`, `POST /backups/restore`. |
| `export` | Taking data out in bulk: `POST /exports`, `GET /exports/:id/download`, `GET /backups/:id/download`, `GET /workspaces/:id/export`. Listing exports and backups and reading one's status is `read`. |
| `all` | All of the above. |

Examples: `dashboards/users read write` reads and changes portal users and nothing else; `dashboards/all read` reads everything and changes nothing; `dashboards/admin export` downloads exports and backups. Without the verb the answer is `403 insufficient_scope`, with `{ required, granted }` in `details`. `GET /me` answers any valid token — it is how an integration tests its credential.

> **Breaking change:** `DELETE` no longer accepts `write` — it needs `delete` (or `all`). The purge moved from `POST` to `DELETE /data_purges`, with the same body. The export and import routes above need `export` and `import`; `write` and `read` no longer do. A token issued before has to be issued again with those levels.

### The `X-Workspace-Id` header

An organization can own **several workspaces**, and every route in this API answers for exactly **one**. While the organization has a single workspace the header may be left out; from the second one on it is required. It takes the workspace `id` or its `public_id`, both shown on the dashboard's **Workspaces** page.

It is a **selector, never a permission**: the workspace sent is checked against the token's organization, and a token issued to a person only reaches the workspaces that person has access to.

| Situation | Response |
| :--- | :--- |
| Header missing with more than one workspace | `400` `workspace_required` |
| Workspace of another organization, nonexistent, or malformed id | `403` `unknown_workspace` |
| The token's person has no access to the workspace | `403` `workspace_access_denied` |
| `org` matches no organization | `403` `unknown_organization` |
| Scope not enough for the operation | `403` `insufficient_scope` |

### Example

```bash
curl https://api.dashboards.kobana.com.br/v1/portal_users \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KOBANA_TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Workspace-Id: $KOBANA_WORKSPACE_ID"
```

For command-line testing, export both: `export KOBANA_TOKEN=xxxxxxxx` and `export KOBANA_WORKSPACE_ID=xxxxxxxx`, then paste the documentation's commands into your terminal.

## Listing and Pagination

Every listing endpoint uses **page-number pagination**:

```
GET /v1/portal_users?page=2&per_page=50&sort_by=created_at&sort_order=desc
```

`per_page` goes up to **100** (default `20`). The response carries the items in `data` and, in `meta`, `total`, `page`, `per_page` and `total_pages`.

## Idempotency

`POST`, `PUT` and `PATCH` requests accept the `X-Idempotency-Key` header. Retries with the same key within **24h** return the original result without repeating the operation — safe to retry after a network failure.

```
X-Idempotency-Key: <client-generated-uuid-v4>
```

## Return Codes

The API returns standard HTTP status codes:

| | Code | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ✅ | **200 OK** | Successful request with a response body. |
| ✅ | **201 Created** | Resource created successfully. |
| ✅ | **204 No Content** | Successful request without a response body. |
| ❌ | **400 Bad Request** | Invalid request, usually malformed content. |
| ❌ | **401 Unauthorized** | Missing or invalid access token. |
| ❌ | **403 Forbidden** | API access blocked or user not authorized. |
| ❌ | **404 Not Found** | Resource not found. |
| ❌ | **422 Unprocessable Entity** | Valid request, but the data is not. |
| ❌ | **429 Too Many Requests** | Rate limit reached. |
| ❌ | **500 Internal Server Error** | Internal processing error. Check [server status](https://status.kobana.com.br). |

## Request ID

Every request has an associated identifier in the `Request-Id` response header. This value helps with debugging and auditing — requests and their IDs are available in the system dashboard. Request logs are retained for **30 days**. When opening a support ticket about a specific request, provide the `Request-Id` to speed up the investigation.

## Security

The Kobana API uses **2048-bit SSL** certificates. Every request must use **HTTPS** — calls on port 80 are redirected to 443.

Clients must support `TLSv1.2` or `TLSv1.3` with one of the ciphers: `TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256`, `TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384`, `TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256`, `ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256`, `ECDHE-RSA-AES128-SHA256`, `ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384`, `ECDHE-RSA-CHACHA20-POLY1305`, `ECDHE-RSA-AES256-SHA384`. `TLSv1` and `TLSv1.1` are not supported.

## HTTP Caching

Use HTTP cache headers to reduce load and improve speed. Most responses include `ETag` and/or `Last-Modified` — store these values and send them back on follow-up requests via `If-None-Match` and `If-Modified-Since`. If the resource hasn't changed you'll get `304 Not Modified` — no body, no reprocessing. More info: [HTTP Cache Docs](http://www.mnot.net/cache_docs/).

## Error Handling

5xx errors mean a server failure: **500 Internal Server Error** (application unavailable), **502 Bad Gateway**, **503 Service Unavailable** and **504 Gateway Timeout** (point-in-time infrastructure failures). Your application must catch these and retry the request after a few minutes with backoff. Server status: [https://status.kobana.com.br](https://status.kobana.com.br).
